questions.q: Every piece of Receivables setup is ultimately scoped to which organizational structure?
options: A ledger and a business unit
questions.explain: Receivables setup sits underneath the ledger (from General Ledger) and the business unit it's assigned to; most setup objects are defined per business unit.

questions.q: Where would you go to set up a 2% discount for paying within 10 days?
questions.explain: Payment terms define due dates, installment schedules, and any early-payment discount percentages and periods.

questions.q: Which setup object provides the default accounting for an adjustment or a receipt write-off?
questions.explain: Receivables activities supply default accounting for everything other than the transaction or receipt itself, including adjustments and write-offs.

questions.q: Why must the business unit and its system options exist before you finish setting up a customer account site?
options: Because customer names must be approved by the business unit manager
Because sites are optional and rarely used
Because sites are only needed for credit memos
Because the site ties a customer to a specific business unit's receivables, so that scope must already exist
questions.explain: A customer account site with a bill-to use is how a transaction knows which business unit's receivables it belongs to.

questions.q: Which setup object gives a reusable description and default accounting for a recurring charge entered on a debit memo?
questions.explain: Memo lines are predefined descriptions with default accounting, used on debit memos, on-account credits, and chargebacks.
